stage: E4b development: select informative contexts as well as actions
history: After inspecting E4 development.csv. All earlier attempts retained. This is a new data-acquisition setting: sample from the known unlabeled finite context pool, instead of assuming contexts must arrive uniformly. Rewards remain vulnerable to the same 0.5% arbitrary edits; no trusted reward oracle for the defender.
design: Q_lambda(x,a)=(1-lambda)*P(x)*mu0(a|x)+lambda*Q_disagree(x,a). Q_disagree=.99*max_j|delta_j(x,a)|/sum_xa max_j|delta_j(x,a)|+.01*P(x)*mu0(a|x). All six candidates define Q, unchanged for each three-candidate library.
gates: Same centered DR/Bernstein, corrected and nominal; development initially evaluates deterministic all-real-edit envelopes, then confirmation runs the full adaptive attacks. Importance coefficient delta/(N_contexts*Q). No label information used by Q or bounds.
cost: Report sampled context shift, expected reward cost versus incumbent on those same contexts, maximum rejection-sampling envelope for access through an iid uniform context stream, and actual query count. Active-pool access is an explicit new assumption.
success: Positive certified worst-case utility averaged across ALL six libraries at fixed epsilon .005; freeze confirmation before new seeds. No global Pareto/novelty claim.
